Histograms

Source: vignettes/articles/r-docs/histograms.Rmd
histograms.Rmd

Basic Histogram 

library(plotly.core)

go_figure() |>
  add_histogram(x = rnorm(50))

Normalized Histogram 

library(plotly.core)

go_figure() |>
  add_histogram(x = rnorm(50), histnorm = "probability")

Specify Binning Function 

library(plotly.core)

x <- c("Apples", "Apples", "Apples", "Organges", "Bananas")
y <- c("5", "10", "3", "10", "5")

go_figure() |>
  add_histogram(y = y, x = x, histfunc = "sum") |>
  update_layout(yaxis = go_yaxis(type = "linear"))

Horizontal Histogram 

library(plotly.core)

go_figure() |>
  add_histogram(y = rnorm(50))

Overlaid Histograms 

library(plotly.core)

go_figure() |>
  add_histogram(x = rnorm(500), opacity = 0.6) |>
  add_histogram(x = rnorm(500) + 1, opacity = 0.6) |>
  update_layout(barmode = "overlay")

Stacked Histograms 

library(plotly.core)

go_figure() |>
  add_histogram(x = rnorm(500), opacity = 0.6) |>
  add_histogram(x = rnorm(500) + 1, opacity = 0.6) |>
  update_layout(barmode = "stack")

Cumulative Histogram 

library(plotly.core)

go_figure() |>
  add_histogram(
    x = rnorm(50),
    cumulative = go_histogram_cumulative(enabled = TRUE)
  )

Share bins between histograms

In this example both histograms have a compatible bin settings using the bingroup attribute (see go_histogram()).

library(plotly.core)

go_figure() |>
  add_histogram(x = rnorm(100, 5), bingroup = 1) |>
  add_histogram(x = rnorm(20, 5), bingroup = 1) |>
  update_layout(barmode = "overlay", bargap = 0.1)

Note that traces on the same subplot, and with the same barmode (“stack”, “relative”, “group”) are forced into the same bingroup, however traces with barmode = "overlay" and on different axes (of the same axis type) can have compatible bin settings. Histogram and histogram2d trace can share the same bingroup.

library(plotly.core)

go_figure() |>
  add_histogram(x = rnorm(100, 5)) |>
  add_histogram(x = rnorm(20, 5)) |>
  update_layout(barmode = "stack", bargap = 0.1)

Reference

See go_histogram() for more information and chart attribute options!
